node.title: Re^3: perlbrew: Command [ ... ] terminated with exit code 0 ($? = 13)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
But if I try with slightly changed line: perlbrew exec perl -wle 'print " A" x 1e0 for 1 .. 1e2' | less -S There is no warning, although I didn't scroll the whole output.

perl -wle 'print " A" x 1e0 for 1 .. 1e2' is 300 bytes, while perl -wle 'print " A" x 1e3 for 1 .. 1e2' is 200100 bytes. Since you're piping the output of perl to another program, perl's output isn't line-based (see e.g. [https://perl.plover.com/FAQs/Buffering.html|Suffering from Buffering]), and so what I'm fairly certain is happening is that perl is simply outputting the 300 bytes in one go. Update: Because perl -wle '$|++; print " A" x 1e0 for 1 .. 1e2' isn't killed by SIGPIPE either, it may also have something to do with how much data a pipe can buffer, but I'm not an expert on that.
